ChromaticShiftCorrectionTest.pins: chromatic shift correction (demo_useful_tools.m) with integer voxel offsets. Both channels image the same synthetic scene; channel c voxel i shows scene voxel i + offset(c, :), so after correction the channels must be identical where they overlap.

fullModeContainsBothChannels.pins: 'full' mode used to size the output from the bounding box starts and flip the offsets

memAllocateIsInGigabytes.pins: 979fa55 regression: memAllocate (GB) was computed in bytes, so every Slurm job requested the maximum number of CPUs

offsetsEstimatedFromPSFs.pins: without chromaticOffset, offsets are measured from bead images (one per channel) of the same beads

sameModeKeepsImageSize.pins: 'same' mode used to error (neworigin undefined), flip the offsets and shift the output by half the image by default

FFTSpectrumTest.pins: XR_fftSpectrumComputingWrapper ("FFT analysis" in demo_useful_tools.m). A cosine along x with an integer number of periods has a power spectrum with exactly three nonzero peaks, so the outputs can be checked analytically.

evenSizeThatNeedsCropOrPadErrors.pins: the center of an even outSize was never defined: cropping or padding the resized image to it errors

matchesWholeSpectrumComputation.pins: only the region of the resized image that is kept is resized, and the MIPs and central slices come from the unshifted |FFT| with the normalization and gamma applied to them: the same values as from the whole resized image and shifted spectrum

resamplesAnisotropicVoxels.pins: input with dz = 2 * xyPixelSize is resampled to isotropic voxels of outPixelSize before the FFT, so the output size is outSize regardless of the input size

spectrumOfCosineHasExpectedPeaks.pins: spectrum of cosine has expected peaks

FSCAnalysisTest.pins: XR_FSC_analysis_wrapper ("FSC analysis" in demo_useful_tools.m), which runs Fourier shell correlation on decon iterations (Iter_*.tif) to pick the number of iterations. The single-image FSC correlates interleaved sub-lattices of the image, so it measures the noise-limited resolution: the same structure with more noise (as with too many decon iterations) must get a worse (larger) resolution value.

oneImageMatchesResizingTheWholeImage.pins: only the region kept after the isotropic resize is resized (from the input region it depends on); the FSC must equal that of resizing the whole image and cropping it

resultIsMovedIntoPlace.pins: the job framework counts a task as done once its result exists, and the wrapper loads each result right after it returns; a result saved in place could be read half written

shellCacheFollowsParameters.pins: XR_FSC keeps the window and the frequency shells between calls: the same call twice and calls with another dr, dtheta, skipConeRegion or halfSize must give the results of fresh calls

FlatfieldBackgroundEstimationTest.pins: XR_flatfield_background_wrapper: estimates the camera background from dark (sample free) stacks. Slices noisier than the median slice and slices with bright structures are excluded, so the estimate is the dark level even with some sample content in the stack.

acceptsMccModeFalse.pins: mccMode used to be validated with @ischar

brightSlicesAreExcluded.pins: a bright object in some slices must not raise the estimate

estimateOfAFileInTheCurrentFolderStaysTh.pins: XR_flatfield_background_estimation of a result file name without a folder wrote it and its MIP to the root (fileparts gives no folder); they are in the current folder, the same as for a full path (the MIPs folder is the caller's, as in the wrapper)

ImarisConversionTest.pins: XR_imaris_conversion_data_wrapper ("Imaris converter" in demo_useful_tools.m). It shells out to the bundled Parallel_Imaris_Writer executable for this platform (via system()), so this also checks that the executable and its libraries run.

bboxCropsTheBoxOfTheDefinition.pins: inputBbox is 1-based and inclusive, the converter's -B 0-based and end-exclusive: the crop started one row, column and slice late. The first voxel of the box holds the maximum of the crop; the voxels just before and just past the box hold larger values.

bboxOfTiffInputIsRefused.pins: the bundled converter crops the output of tiff input but not the tiff it reads, which scrambled the image; it is now refused before any output

converterArgumentsHaveNoSpaces.pins: c9f2f9c regression: num2str pads numbers of different widths with spaces ([8, 8, 16] became '8, 8,16,'), which split the converter's -b/-v arguments. The command is captured with a framework spy instead of running the converter.

convertsChannelsAndTimePoints.pins: two channels (8c93f1b regression: with several channel patterns no file was selected) and two time points

filesOfDifferentSizesAreRejected.pins: the converter takes the size of the first file for every time point and channel: a time point of another size is an error (before any output), unless inputBbox crops all to one size

imageSizeIsNotPaddedToBlocks.pins: KNOWN ISSUE: Parallel_Imaris_Writer records the image size padded to multiples of blockSize (48 x 32 x 24 for a 40 x 32 x 20 image with blockSize 16), and its histograms count the padding, so Imaris shows zero borders and a histogram minimum of 0. The ImageSize attributes should be the true size.

masterComputeIsPassedToTheFramework.pins: the wrapper took masterCompute but didn't pass it on, so with false the master still converted (and a master job sized for waiting ran out of memory)

PSFAnalysisTest.pins: XR_psf_analysis_wrapper ("PSF analysis" in demo_useful_tools.m): deskew the PSF, then plot it and its OTF against a Richards & Wolf widefield PSF. Even for a 64 x 64 x 101 PSF this needs ~22 GB of RAM (the plots are simulated on a 1001^3 double grid) and ~80 s, so it is skipped on machines with less than 32 GB (e.g., GitHub runners).

detectionInfoIsMovedIntoPlace.pins: XR_psf_detection_and_analysis_wrapper's tasks count as done once their info file exists, so it must not be saved in place

plotDataMatchWholeGrid.pins: the PSF and OTF on the 1001^3 simulation grid are kept as their data regions (the grid is zero elsewhere); the slices must equal those of the whole grid (the reference needs it)

PunctaRemovalTest.pins: XR_ExM_PunctaRemoval_zarr (expansion microscopy puncta removal): a large stained structure and a few small, very bright puncta on a dark background. The puncta must be removed, the structure kept, and the output must keep the input size.

interpolatedBackgroundOneValueDeepInZ.pins: a background estimated in batches as deep as the volume is one value deep in z, which MATLAB's arrays drop: imresize3 of a batch's background failed (MATLAB:badsubscript). The plane's interpolation is the background at every z, the same as for the plane twice in z

parametersFileHoldsTheParameters.pins: parameters.json was written with its text as fprintf's format: a % in a value (here in the folder name) cut the file off there

punctumAtACornerIsFilledFromTheNearestPi.pins: the linear fill (fillmissing2) left the removed pixels of a punctum at a corner of the image NaN, outside the convex hull of the known pixels, and a later pass on that volume failed in imregionalmax (MATLAB:imregionalmax:expectedNonNaN); they take the value of the nearest pixel, so the fills stay within the values of the pixels that are kept

removesPunctaWithDefaultThresholds.pins: the task string used to be invalid with the default (empty) thresholds, and the block function couldn't handle them

removesPunctaWithScalarThresholds.pins: the task string used to pass parameters the block function doesn't take, and the block called a misspelled function

UnmixChannelsTest.pins: channel unmixing (demo_useful_tools.m, "Channel Unmixing" sections): out = max(0, sum_c factor(c) * (ch_c - constBackground(c))) + constOffset, computed by unmix_channels_sum (unmix_channels_sum_mex in one pass, or the MATLAB code where the mex is missing)

flatFieldCorrectionBeforeUnmixing.pins: 1f40f4c added flat-field correction to unmixing; 824f476 fixed flat-field/background images that are not single (as read from uint16 tiffs), which made the mex reject them and fall back to the slow MATLAB path

frameMatchesTheOriginalCode.pins: the frame function computes the sum in unmix_channels_sum, at once (channels as read that take with the result at most 8 bytes per voxel) or one channel at a time: the same values as the per-channel code it replaced, with flat field correction, gaussian filtering, a channel with factor 0 (not read), backgrounds, offsets, and single channels

gaussianUnmixingBlursTheOtherChannel.pins: 'gaussian' mode filters each channel with its sigma (one row per channel, [sy, sx, sz]) before the weighted sum

gaussianUnmixingThroughDataWrapper.pins: the wrapper used to format the sigma matrix (one row per channel) as a row vector

imagesWithoutAllChannelsAreLeftOut.pins: time points without all channels failed the grouping by channels; their images are left out with a warning, as the wrapper says (and the second folder was grouped with the channels of the first one's files)

largeFileResultsAreTheZarrFilesOfTheTask.pins: with largeFile the tasks (XR_unmix_channels_zarr) write zarr, also without saveZarr, but the wrapper gave the job framework .tif results: it waited for files no task writes and ran each task three times (about 6 minutes even in local mode)

largeFileTasksRunOnce.pins: (as above) the job framework finds the result of a large-file task after its first run

memAllocateIsInGigabytes.pins: 979fa55 regression: memAllocate (GB) was computed in bytes, so every Slurm job requested the maximum number of CPUs

mexMatchesTheMatlabCode.pins: uint8, uint16, single and double channels (single and double with NaN, Inf, -0, huge values and values that round at .5), mixed, with backgrounds and offsets (also 0, NaN and single), factors and backgrounds that single can't represent, 0 and Inf; 3D, 2D, a vector, sizes around the mex's blocks of 8192, more blocks than threads, and empty

otherClassesUseTheMatlabCode.pins: other channel and result classes are computed in MATLAB, without a mex fallback

partialSumsGiveTheSameResult.pins: channels added one at a time to a partial sum (dtype empty), then clipped, offset and cast (no channels and the sum), give the result of one call, bit for bit: uint8, uint16, double and single channels (single ones are added in place by MATLAB), with the mex and with the MATLAB code

sumRoundsAsMatlab.pins: products with a double factor and a double offset are rounded to single once (not computed in single), sums in single, cast rounds half away from zero (0.49999997 is 0, uint16() gives 1) and saturates, NaN and negative sums are 0

zarrBlocksMatchTheOriginalCode.pins: the linear and gaussian zarr block functions with batches that don't divide the image, as the per-channel code they replaced: uint16 channels summed at once, filtered and single channels one at a time

zarrFunctionKeepsResultOfAnotherRun.pins: a copy from another run (its own uuid) that finds the result published replaced it with its own, incomplete result

zarrFunctionMatchesFrameFunction.pins: XR_unmix_channels_zarr ("Channel Unmixing for Zarr Files") processes in batches; small batches must give the same result
